target_claim: The proof claims that because S = {m, m+1, ..., m+n-1} contains a multiple of j for each j = 1..n, the product of the elements of S can be regrouped as (k_1 * 1)(k_2 * 2)...(k_n * n), i.e. the n elements of S can be matched one-to-one with the factors 1, 2, ..., n so that each element is a multiple of its assigned factor. This simultaneous/distinct-representative regrouping does not follow from the cited lemma and is false in general.
source_quote: | r = k_1 2 k_2 3 k_3 \dotsm \paren {n - 1} k_{n - 1} n k_n
